compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar resolves configuration through multiple authorities during one operation, and some backends reread ambient state after receiving explicit config. Authentication is also composed inconsistently across LLM, Git, bridge, MCP, review-bot, observability, and op-cert boundaries. This can change behavior mid-operation, discard an explicit choice, expose static credentials to unrelated children, or fall back through an unintended identity. RP-04 establishes one application-wide composition contract without making Rebar a credential store.

The approved research, probes, and decision trail are on `relevant-liberal-xantus` and in `.joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md`, `.joe-janitor/rp04-composition-readback.md`, and `.joe-janitor/rp04-adr-research-critique.md`.

## Approved design
- Resolve one immutable, serializable, non-secret `OperationSnapshot` at each operation boundary. Precedence is explicit operation input > environment > project config > user config > schema default.
- Resolve repository root separately: explicit `repo_root` > `REBAR_ROOT` > Git top-level/current directory. Interpret winning relative paths against that root.
- CLI composes once per invocation; MCP and Python once per operation; long-running processes also own startup deployment policy and live runtime bindings. An in-progress operation does not reread environment, files, cwd, or global config.
- Compose subsystem-local `GitRuntime`, `LLMRuntime`, and selected `BridgeRuntime` bindings. Provider SDKs/helpers own credential issuance, storage, refresh, expiry, invalidation, and native precedence. Rebar-owned factories accept provider-native pre-client auth/session capabilities and retain Rebar retry, timeout, cache, output, error, and lifecycle policy. Arbitrary public constructed-client/runner replacement is initially out of scope.
- Represent unavoidable static material with provider-specific, non-serializable Pydantic `SecretStr`/`SecretBytes` carriers, revealing it only in the sending adapter. Do not add a universal secret broker, central credential union, automatic keyring fallback, or application-owned cloud-secret retrieval.
- Trusted same-capability children inherit ambient environment for Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA compatibility. Rebar never installs credentials through global `os.environ` mutation. An owning child receives its adapter overlay; unrelated sibling children remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters. Deployment/container/process boundaries remain the primary isolation mechanism.
- Static bindings rotate on restart/redeploy; SDK-native refresh remains SDK-owned.
- Op-cert accepts exactly one of `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` (preferred) or `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY`, validates before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, and copies the key into a process-owned 0700 directory/0600 file. Jobs receive context-local signer/principal/push-policy bindings. Remove runtime SSM/boto3/region coupling and per-job retrieval. Deployment may retain ADR 0049's SSM-at-rest source by injecting/mounting the resolved secret before process startup.
- Fail closed when explicit provider/profile/project/auth composition fails; never retry anonymously or as another ambient principal. Preserve optional write-only Langfuse/OTLP observability's fail-open/no-op behavior.

## Scope
RP-04 only: central non-secret resolution/provenance, operation projections, runtime bindings, provider-native auth injection, static-secret handling, op-cert startup composition, all affected CLI/library/MCP/reconciler/hosted consumers, ownership gates, generated operator documentation, migration, and canaries. RP-02/RP-03 and RP-05/RP-06 remain separate.

Explicit behavior corrections include: explicit CLI input outranks environment for `tracker.dir`; malformed operation config fails before lock/network/write; backend properties remain stable after construction; supplied Python config is not ambiently re-overlaid; effective defaults live in the central schema; tracker directory/branch/remote reaches every owner; and Jira Cloud write scope has no `DIG` fallback. Existing auth-failure, redaction, retry, TLS, and output lessons remain unless a child ticket names and tests a deliberate change.

## Migration / rollback
Use expand-contract sequencing: add snapshots/projections and runtime bindings in shadow mode; prove precedence, lifecycle, fingerprints, and non-leakage; adapt factories/consumers in call-graph slices behind compatibility facades; add structural gates and generated docs; run hosted canaries; then remove legacy composition. Before write cutover, disable shadow composition to roll back. During expansion, facades may delegate to legacy composition. After cutover, rollback requires a compatibility floor that understands the snapshot envelope. RP-04 changes no stored ticket or bridge format. Never persist or log credentials while diagnosing parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI, MCP, Python, and direct reconciler paths produce equivalent non-secret behavior from the approved precedence/root contract; a captured operation is stable across environment/file/cwd mutation while the next operation observes the change.
- [ ] Every affected consumer receives an immutable projection/runtime binding; structural checks find no ambient config/credential reads, backend reloads, or configurable hard-coded defaults below approved composition seams.
- [ ] LLM, Git, and bridge factories preserve provider-native auth lifecycles and instantiate only the selected integration; missing/conflicting decision-bearing auth fails before network/write without anonymous, cross-provider, or alternate-principal fallback.
- [ ] Secret canaries are absent from repr, equality/hash, serialization, snapshots, fingerprints, caches, provenance, exceptions, logs, output, argv, URL/query strings, subprocess siblings, and CLI/MCP schemas, verified at behavioral boundaries.
- [ ] Same-capability children preserve unknown ambient/native-chain variables, owning children receive only their overlay, unrelated siblings lose exact Rebar-declared secret names, and concurrent operations observe no global environment mutation.
- [ ] Op-cert enforces its exclusive startup sources, fails invalid composition before service work, uses a stable process-owned 0700/0600 copy and context-local signer, observes replacement only after restart, deletes only its copy, and has no application runtime SSM/boto3/region dependency.
- [ ] Generated config/security/operator docs cover precedence, lifecycles, restart/redeploy rotation, provider ownership, observability's exception, subprocess limitations, and deliberate behavior deltas; drift checks detect schema/docs divergence.
- [ ] Legacy ambient/per-job composition is removed only after focused suites and bounded live paths pass; rollback retains accurate non-secret diagnostics.
- [ ] [operator-attested] AWS review-bot and reconciler check/dry-run/bounded-live canaries pass after cutover without credential leakage or unauthorized fallback. Epic comments record run/change IDs, timestamps, selected provider/auth-source kind, retry counts, and redacted outcomes.

## Sequencing
The ADR child records and critiques this approved boundary first. Create implementation children only after the ADR reaches HOLD/MERGE; make them vertical, independently reviewable slices ordered by real artifacts, each with behavioral oracles and exact file impact. Do not review or claim this epic until that child graph exists.
